# NSPanel HAUI 0.4.2

NSPanel HAUI 0.4.2 completes the update path. The panel can now install its own
firmware update, a release no longer needs a Nextion Editor visit just to change
the version, and the TFT reinstall loop and buzzer bugs reported by users are
fixed.

## Before updating

- **The ESPHome web server is no longer enabled by default** — the shipped
  firmware leaves out `web_server` to free the flash and RAM that the HTTP OTA
  path (TLS, JSON, `http_request`) needs. After flashing the new firmware the
  device's web UI on port 80 and Home Assistant's **Visit** link disappear
  until you enable the component yourself: add a `web_server:` block to your
  own device YAML (see
  [ESPHome Component → Web server](docs/esphome.md#web-server-optional)).
  `esphome/nspanel_haui_dev.yaml` keeps the web server for local development.
- **Flash the new firmware once manually** — the **HAUI Firmware** entity only
  exists from 0.4.2 on, so an older firmware cannot be updated by the hub.
  After that first flash, later firmware updates can come through Home
  Assistant.
- **The release's TFTs already contain the display fixes** — a TFT auto-update
  installs them; rebuilding the TFTs from the HMI yourself is only needed if
  you maintain a custom build.

## New

- **Firmware auto-update** — the release workflow now attaches a
  `firmware-manifest.json` to every release and the firmware exposes an
  `update: platform: http_request` entity named **HAUI Firmware**. When the hub
  finds a newer release and `firmware_auto_update` is on (the default), it asks
  Home Assistant to install the device's firmware update first; the TFT the new
  firmware needs is installed after the device reboots. A running TFT upload is
  never interrupted — the firmware install waits for it to finish. Set
  `firmware_auto_update: false` to keep the previous notice-only behaviour.
- **Version bump tooling** — `scripts/bump_version.py` updates the manifest,
  `pyproject.toml`, ESPHome `version.yaml` and both HMI `system.tftVersion`
  values in one command, so a release no longer needs a Nextion Editor visit
  just to type the new version. The HMI edit is in place and only legal for a
  same-length version; a length-changing bump still needs the Editor.
  `scripts/bump_tft_version.py` bumps only the HMI text and is reused by the
  combined script. Both have a `--check` dry run and are covered by
  `tests/test_bump_version.py`.

## Changed

- **Update checks install the firmware first** — when a newer release exists
  and the device reports an installable firmware update, the hub triggers the
  firmware install before the TFT. The device reboots into the new firmware and
  then installs the matching TFT on the next connect. Set
  `firmware_auto_update: false` to restore the notice-only behaviour.
- **CI validates version consistency and translations** — the tests workflow
  checks that the version sources agree (`scripts/bump_version.py --check`) and
  that translation files are up to date; the release workflow rejects a tag
  whose version disagrees with `manifest.json`, so a release cannot ship a
  mismatched version. The tests workflow also validates the Nextion assets and
  runs `ruff` on `scripts/`.

## Fixed

- **Firmware display reads work on released ESPHome again** — the
  numeric-response delivery fix for the stock `nextion` component
  ([esphome PR #17744](https://github.com/esphome/esphome/pull/17744)) was
  merged two days after the 2026.10.0 release tag was cut, so *no released
  ESPHome* contains it; without it every display read logged
  `Numeric return but '…' invalid type 0` and the value was dropped (`page` /
  `dim` errors after every interaction, lost `res_val`/`res_txt`/TFT-version
  reads). The firmware configs now ship a temporary vendored patch
  (`esphome/nextion_patch/`, the 2026.10.0 component plus the cherry-picked
  fix) and override the stock component with it through `external_components`
  — shipped in the `nspanel_haui.yaml` package, so installed setups pick it up
  with their next `esphome config` run; the universal/dev configs use a local
  source so CI and the release build validate the actual checkout. Recompile
  and flash the firmware once. The patch and its override blocks are removed
  (and `min_version` raised) when a released ESPHome contains #17744.
- **TFT no longer reinstalls after every reboot
  ([#63](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/issues/63))** — the hub
  compared the firmware's `yaml_version` against the `tft_version` snapshot
  captured during the boot handshake, when the display had not answered yet.
  The empty value parsed as `0.0.0`, so the hub considered the TFT outdated,
  uploaded it, rebooted the ESP32, and repeated the loop. An unknown version is
  now treated as *unknown*: the hub requests a fresh device state and only
  evaluates known versions. A recent unconfirmed install is no longer
  auto-retried — use **Install TFT** in the editor to retry manually. The
  `INSTALLING` state now survives the reboot, and a matching version reported
  on reconnect marks the install `done`.
- **Buzzer stops when a TFT upload starts
  ([#62](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/issues/62))** —
  `upload_tft()` blocks the ESP32 main loop for the whole transfer, so a
  playing RTTTL tune never had its note turned off and kept sounding until the
  reboot. The three upload entry points (the Update Display button and the
  `upload_tft`/`upload_tft_url` actions) now run a shared `suspend_activities`
  script first, which stops the buzzer; future stoppable components only need
  to be added there. Flash the updated ESPHome firmware to activate the fix.
- **Portrait weather time and date are centred
  ([#64](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/issues/64))** — the
  full-width portrait `tTime`/`tDate` widgets kept the landscape
  right-alignment attribute and drew against the screen edge. `PORTRAIT_ATTRS`
  now centres them in the portrait TFT.
- **Failed TFT installs report why** — the update controller returns its state
  (idle/checking/installing/error/done) from `install_tft`/`run_update_display`,
  the REST API responds with HTTP 502 and the editor shows a toast when the
  upload command could not be sent. A GitHub API failure during the update
  check no longer raises out of the timer callback.

## Issues addressed

- [#62](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/issues/62) — buzzer keeps
  sounding through a TFT upload. Thanks to [@jsenecal](https://github.com/jsenecal).
- [#63](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/issues/63) — TFT reinstalls
  after every panel reboot. Thanks to [@jsenecal](https://github.com/jsenecal).
- [#64](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/issues/64) — portrait weather
  time and date are right-aligned. Thanks to [@jsenecal](https://github.com/jsenecal).
